title: Moral relativism is a disputed metaethical position
summary: Baghramian and Carter's entry maps the arguments. It does not declare relativism true or false.
body: Maria Baghramian and J. Adam Carter's Stanford Encyclopedia entry on relativism distinguishes descriptive claims (people differ) from philosophical claims (there is no stance-independent moral truth). The v1 article asks whether moral truths are universal. That question is open in the sense that competent philosophers still defend both sides. A list of cultural differences does not, by itself, answer it.

contested_views.label: Philosophical
contested_views.summary: The same entry distinguishes the claim that there is no stance-independent moral truth. This card says competent philosophers still defend both sides of whether moral truths are universal, and it names no winner.
